state.case_summary:
A 42-year-old patient with night blindness since childhood. The patient has been followed for 30 years, with initial presentation at age 10. The patient reports no symptoms except night blindness and is unaware of field loss. Past medical history is unremarkable.

- Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)- Color vision: Normal- Fundus examination: Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration- Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades- Goldmann visual field: Inferonasal scotoma

1. Electroretinogram (ERG):- Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses- Flat rod electroretinogram- Lower amplitudes compared to 30 years ago2. Fundus Autofluorescence:- Superotemporal zones showing hypofluorescence- Narrow hyperfluorescent ring inside- Central macula appears unremarkable3. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT):- Central macula: Clear OCT layers- Perifoveal region: Supernormal thickness (beyond 99%)- Parafoveal region: 95% thickness- Foveal region: Normal thickness- Eccentric areas: Marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization- Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

root.label: Chronic Progressive Night Blindness with Scotopic and Photopic Electroretinogram Abnormalities

alarm_features: Chronic and progressive nature of symptoms
salient_findings: Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
